sampling_model.design: One random sample of \(n\) independent bounded-window vectors; causal randomness and inferential sampling randomness are kept distinct.
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes one binary vector in \(\{0,1\}^{\mathcal W_H}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The focal treatment is \(X_{-\gamma}\); the causal estimand compares two interventions while fixing the common possible-parent set \(Z\) at \(z\).
sampling_model.overlap: The collapse and strict-separation results use a strictly positive observed-window law; the general sharp compiler, empty-fiber certification, and confidence-fiber program permit probability-simplex boundary cells.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The multinomial vector \(p\) is estimated by \(\widehat p\); all causal endpoints and same-SCM pairwise contrasts are reoptimized over one simultaneous rational box-simplex region.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their controlled-effect theorem identifies the micro CDE by an unadjusted conditional-mean contrast when the outcome is in no nontrivial directed cycle and has no bidirected edge to a directed ancestor.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The positive-lag frontier theorem proves that the bounded-window micro condition is necessary and sufficient for this unadjusted contrast to equal the CDE uniformly over every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model in the present class. The one-lag \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) witness shows a strict gain over the label-level exclusion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their response-function construction turns one specified discrete causal model into a polynomial program and obtains numerical valid bounds converging to sharpness.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The sharp-envelope and exact-certification theorems compile the union of all observationally feasible positive-lag refinements, attain both endpoints, reconstruct endpoint SCMs, and return exact algebraic certificates.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their causal-order linear program optimizes counterfactual queries over arbitrary masses on complete deterministic response signatures consistent with the supplied order and reconstructs attaining SCMs.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The order-tightening theorem uses their unrestricted complete-order model as an outer comparator, while the quotient-obstruction theorem shows that arbitrary quotient masses cannot replace independent edge-factor weights in the present semi-Markovian refinement compiler.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.1 preserves a canonical-domain linear program by pushing an unrestricted simplex mass to equivalence cells and selecting one raw representative per cell for the reverse lift.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The quotient-obstruction theorem separates that unrestricted-simplex setting from the present independent-edge-latent setting: a full-support rational quotient law violates a factor-incidence polynomial satisfied by every raw product model.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their bounded-segment theorem decides identification in one known periodic bounded-lag ADMG by cutting repeated hedge states.
Their PAG procedure gives sound analytical bounds at least as tight as natural bounds and shows that several graph representatives may remain necessary.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The robust order-tightening theorem gives an explicit temporal micro-CDE family on which summary-graph refinement bounds are strictly narrower than the complete-order outer comparator.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their covering-collection construction gives uniformly valid minimum-average-volume confidence regions for a multinomial parameter.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The simultaneous whole-set inference theorem propagates one multinomial confidence event through all endpoint and same-SCM contrast optimizations.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their root-cause method compares identified direct effects under an acyclic causally sufficient summary graph.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The simultaneous whole-set inference theorem extends comparison to partially identified refinement fibers and reports ties whenever the same-SCM difference interval contains zero.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their real-quantifier-elimination results give arithmetic-operation bounds and output degree and coefficient-size bounds in polynomial count, degree, coefficient height, and variable blocks.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The exact-certification theorem applies those direct arithmetic and size bounds to the causal compiler; its stated bit-operation bound is the derived corollary obtained from the accompanying bit-size control, not a separately quoted source theorem.

body.tldr: A finite binary process is observed through a bounded window and a lag-abstracted directed and bidirected summary graph. Directed effects occur only at positive lags through \(L\), while bidirected dependence may span any summary-compatible pair of time points in the observed \(H\)-window. The sharp controlled-micro-direct-effect envelope is the attained range of the raw semi-Markovian polynomial programs over exactly those refinements whose canonical fiber reproduces the observed law; a total exact certifier returns either branchwise incompatibility evidence or isolated algebraic endpoints with attaining SCMs. In the present independent pairwise-edge-latent class, the bounded-window micro condition is necessary and sufficient for the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast to equal the micro CDE uniformly over every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model. This is an exact frontier for that contrast, not a necessary-and-sufficient identification criterion from the full observed law. The condition permits directed summary cycles through \(Y\) and strictly improves the label-level exclusion, as witnessed by the one-lag summary \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\). The envelope is strictly narrower on a relative-open temporal-instrument family than a complete temporal-order comparator, and simultaneous multinomial regions support tie-aware inference. Exact response-signature analysis preserves the image under factorized push-forward, supplies a quotient-size bound and a factor-incidence test, and gives a full-support rational obstruction showing that unrestricted quotient masses erase independent edge-factor incidence; the endpoint compiler therefore retains the raw product parameterization unless the test succeeds.

project_justification.gap: Existing summary-graph adjustment results give sufficient label-level conditions in broader models that may contain contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws; they do not give the exact finite-window frontier for uniform validity of the unadjusted conditional-mean contrast in a positive-lag independent-edge-latent class. Existing automated bounds generally treat one declared graph. Moreover, unrestricted response-signature simplex reductions do not encode the nonlinear incidence constraints imposed by mutually independent overlapping pairwise latent parents, and their failure could previously be dismissed as a boundary-support artifact.
project_justification.niche: The positive-directed-lag bound makes the full-time refinement set finite and makes \(Y_0\) terminal, while summary-compatible bidirected lags remain unrestricted inside the observed window. The bounded positive-lag supergraph exposes exactly when a latent incident to \(Y_0\) can enter the recursive determination of the controlled possible-parent vector. Binary canonical response functions turn every observationally feasible fixed-refinement image into a compact semialgebraic set; the complete temporal-order common-latent model remains a coherent graph-free outer comparator. Retaining the independent latent-factor product structure distinguishes this compiler from unrestricted response-signature simplexes.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a sharp raw compiler over all and only observationally feasible refinements, proves endpoint attainment and SCM reconstruction, and gives a total exact certifier. It proves that the bounded-window micro condition holds if and only if the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast is uniformly correct over every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model in this class; the one-lag \(B\to X\to Y\), \(Y\leftrightarrow B\) example certifies strict improvement over the label-level exclusion. It separately records that failure of the condition need not destroy identification from the full observed law. Explicit rational primal tables, pointwise dual inequalities, and an interior ledger certify relative-open strict tightening, while one multinomial event is propagated through all queries and contrasts. For response-signature compression, exact factorized push-forward fidelity, a necessary-and-sufficient factor-incidence sentence, a quotient-size bound, and the full-support parity-tilt obstruction explain precisely when unrestricted quotienting is unsound. The exact-elimination analysis uses direct arithmetic-operation and output-size bounds; the bit-operation statement is their derived corollary.

body.related_work: Ferreira and Assaad (2026, Theorem 9) provide the summary-graph controlled-micro-direct-effect setup and an unadjusted conditional-mean identifying expression under label-level graphical conditions. In the present finite-window binary semi-Markovian class with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents, strict positive lags make \(Y_0\) terminal. The new bounded-window micro condition is exact for a deliberately narrower uniform claim: it holds if and only if \(q(\mathcal M)=A_{\mathrm{FA}}(P_{\mathcal M})\) for every admissible refinement and every strictly positive model in this class. It removes the singleton strongly connected component requirement and the conservative exclusion of every summary bidirected edge to a summary ancestor. With \(H=L=1\), summary arrows \(B\to X\to Y\), and \(Y\leftrightarrow B\), the only \(B\to X\) placement is too late to affect controlled parent \(X_{-1}\), so the new condition holds although the label-level exclusion fails. This exactness concerns the unadjusted Ferreira--Assaad contrast, not identification from the entire observed law: with \(H=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), \(B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\to Y_0\), and \(B_{-2}\leftrightarrow Y_0\), the micro condition fails but adjustment for observed \(B_{-2}\) can still identify the effect. The present scope neither contains nor is contained in Ferreira--Assaad's broader one, because they permit contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws while this paper excludes instantaneous directed effects and imposes independent pairwise-edge-latent factorization. Duarte et al. (2024, Propositions 1--2 and Algorithm 2) provide the canonical response-function and polynomialization method adapted within each refinement; the present sharp union ranges only over refinements with a nonempty canonical fiber, and the total exact real-algebraic layer adds branchwise incompatibility certificates, endpoint isolation, causal-size bounds, and decoded SCM witnesses. Jahn, Karnik, and Schulman (2025, Propositions 1--2) inform finite-window reasoning for known bounded-lag periodic ADMGs but are not the source of the positive-lag restriction. Rossetto and Antonucci (2026) and Choe et al. (2026) use unrestricted masses on response signatures or equivalence cells. Here push-forward is exact only while the induced factorized quotient family is retained: for rational \(0<\theta<1\), the full-support law \(p_\theta(w)=2^{-N}[1+\theta(-1)^{A_0\mathbin\oplus C_0}]\) belongs to an unrestricted quotient simplex, while the raw independent-edge-latent image satisfies \(F(P)=P_{00}P_{11}-P_{01}P_{10}=0\) and the displayed law has \(F(P)=\theta/4\). Thus the obstruction is not caused by zero observational cells. A finite factor-incidence sentence decides equality, lexicographic minimization gives a semialgebraic selector when equality holds, and the derived quotient-size bound closes the former size question. Evans (2016, Theorem 4.13 and Proposition 7.4) motivates retaining latent-margin structure. Geiger and Meek (1999) and Basu, Pollack, and Roy (1996) supply exact-elimination and complexity ancestors; the arithmetic-operation and output bit-size bounds are used directly, while the theorem's bit-operation complexity is the resulting derived corollary. Bellot (2024, Propositions 3--5) shows that partial graphical information can improve graph-free bounds but does not give the present temporal micro-CDE strictness region. Malloy, Tripathy, and Nowak (2020, Theorem 1) motivate whole-multinomial coverage, while Assaad, Ez-Zejjari, and Zan (2023, Proposition 7 and Theorem 1) supply the downstream direct-effect root-cause comparison made uncertainty-aware by the same-SCM tie rule.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Exact push-forward to response-signature equivalence classes preserves the raw image when the induced factorized quotient family is retained, but this operation alone does not remove the latent product parameterization. The unrestricted branchwise quotient simplex is computationally smaller and is not sound in general. On the edge-latent-chain instance, the rational family \(p_\theta(w)=2^{-N}[1+\theta(-1)^{A_0\mathbin\oplus C_0}]\), \(0<\theta<1\), has every observed cell positive but violates by \(\theta/4\) the independence determinant that vanishes on the raw image. The exact factor-incidence test decides graph by graph whether the unrestricted quotient happens to be safe, and the canonical catalogue has a derived finite quotient-size bound. Consequently the certified endpoint compiler retains raw product weights unless that test succeeds; the remaining limitation is worst-case combinatorial size, not unresolved fidelity, support, or quotient size.
body.honest_scope: The paper studies finite-window binary SCMs with mutually independent private and pairwise edge latents. It excludes instantaneous directed effects and directed lags beyond \(L\), but places no \(L\)-bound on bidirected lags inside the observed \(H\)-window. Ferreira--Assaad allow contemporaneous arrows and general joint exogenous laws, so the positive-lag theorem is an extension only within the present distinct scope. Its necessary-and-sufficient claim is exactly a frontier for uniform equality with the unadjusted contrast \(A_{\mathrm{FA}}\), not a necessary-and-sufficient criterion for identification from the full observed law. Indeed, with \(H=2\), \(L=\gamma=1\), summary arrows \(B\to X\to Y\), and \(B\leftrightarrow Y\), a refinement containing \(B_{-2}\to X_{-1}\to Y_0\) and \(B_{-2}\leftrightarrow Y_0\) fails the micro condition, yet the observed \(B_{-2}\) supplies an alternative adjustment route under the usual positivity needed for that conditional formula. The envelope is the smallest closed interval containing all attainable CDE values; the attainable set itself need not be connected. Its nested extrema range only over refinements whose canonical feasible set is nonempty. No stationarity or infinite-history reduction is assumed. Exact certification is worst-case singly exponential in the raw response-weight dimension and is a certificate engine, not a polynomial-time method. Its arithmetic-operation and output bit-size controls come directly from real-algebraic elimination results; its bit-operation complexity is a derived corollary. Empty fibers receive exact branchwise infeasibility certificates, while nonempty fibers receive attained algebraic endpoints and decoded SCMs. Every graph refinement embeds in the complete temporal-order common-latent comparator, but unrestricted comparator masses are not asserted to respect missing bidirected edges. Strict tightening is relative to positive laws with a nonempty summary-graph fiber. The quotient question is resolved: factorized push-forward is exact, a necessary-and-sufficient real-algebraic test characterizes when the unrestricted quotient simplex is also exact, a finite quotient-size bound is proved, and a full-support rational edge-latent-chain witness shows that unrestricted quotienting fails in general. Accordingly the main compiler remains unquotiented unless the exact test certifies a particular graph. When the refinement class is a singleton the construction reduces to a fixed-graph response program.
